answer: Pay graders by peer prediction instead of headcount. On each pulse, every grader also predicts how others will score the same answer, and it earns only when its verdict turns out more common than the crowd predicted. Independent agents surface real signal that way. A river of clones driven by one model predicts its own verdict perfectly, so its agreement is never surprising and earns nothing; each added copy is just another ripple on the same current, costing compute but adding no reward or vote weight.
